protocol.name: dashi_chrome_v1

description.summary: window chrome and glass for Dashi's surfaces

protocol.description:
Dashi-private. By default dashi-comp draws a title bar above every window that accepts server-side decorations. This protocol lets an app put its own content in that strip: with the "unified" style there is no title bar, the window's surface runs up to the top edge, and the compositor draws only its traffic lights (close, minimize, zoom) over the surface at the top-left.
The app moves the window itself with xdg_toplevel.move from its empty toolbar areas, and zooms it from a double click with xdg_toplevel.set_maximized / unset_maximized. A press on a traffic light goes to the compositor, never to the surface.
Since version 2 it also says what ext-background-effect-v1's blur region cannot: for each pane of glass on a surface, its corner radius and its material (dashi_glass_v1).

interface.name: dashi_chrome_manager_v1

description.summary: creates window chrome controls and glass

interface.description: A global that makes a dashi_chrome_v1 for an xdg_toplevel and, since version 2, a dashi_glass_v1 for any wl_surface.

entry.name: chrome_exists
entry.summary: the toplevel already has a dashi_chrome_v1

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a dashi_glass_v1

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Chrome and glass objects it made stay valid.

request.name: get_chrome

description.summary: get the chrome of a toplevel

request.description: Make the chrome object of `toplevel`. A toplevel has at most one; a second request is a chrome_exists protocol error until the first is destroyed.

request.name: get_glass

description.summary: get the glass of a surface

request.description: Make the glass object of `surface` (a toplevel's, a layer surface's, a popup's or a lock surface's). A surface has at most one; a second request is a glass_exists protocol error until the first is destroyed.

interface.name: dashi_chrome_v1
interface.description:
Sets how the compositor frames one toplevel. Destroying the object puts the toplevel back to the standard style.
The style is read when the window first has a size and follows later changes, but set it before the first commit to avoid a visible shift: the compositor places the surface where the unified or standard layout puts it.

entry.name: standard
entry.summary: the compositor's title bar above the surface

entry.name: unified
entry.summary: no title bar; traffic lights over the surface

request.name: set_style
request.description: The compositor honors "unified" only for windows it would decorate itself: the toplevel has no xdg_toplevel_decoration, or its mode is server_side. An app that asked for client_side draws all of it. When the style is not honored, the controls event reports an empty rectangle.

event.name: controls

description.summary: the area of the traffic lights

event.description:
The rectangle, in surface-local logical coordinates, that the traffic lights occupy including their margins. Leave it empty (no buttons, no text) and start toolbar content past it; the compositor draws over it and takes presses in it.
Sent when the style takes effect or stops, and again when the rectangle changes (for example with the output's scale). A rectangle with zero width and height means there are no controls: the style is standard, or unified was not honored.

interface.name: dashi_glass_v1

description.summary: the panes of glass on one surface

interface.description:
A surface's glass: rounded rectangles of it the compositor fills with a material (what is behind, blurred, saturated and tinted, with grain, a rim and a hairline, as the shell's look for that material says) instead of the surface's own pixels there, which the client leaves clear.
It goes with ext-background-effect-v1. The client sets the blur region (ext_background_effect_surface_v1.set_blur_region) to the union of its panes, rounded as a wl_region allows, and the panes here with their exact radius and material, both before the same wl_surface.commit. The compositor draws each pane clipped to the blur region; a pane outside it shows no glass. A surface with a blur region and no panes (any app that speaks only ext-background-effect-v1) is glass of the regular material, the region's shape, at the compositor's corner radius for windows.
Whether glass is drawn at all is ext-background-effect-v1's blur capability (ext_background_effect_manager_v1.capabilities): without it the client paints its own fill under each pane, and when it comes or goes the client paints again. The compositor's own fallbacks (an opaque twin for Reduce Transparency or a GPU that cannot blur, the wallpaper only on battery saver) keep the capability: they are still drawn in the panes, so the client still leaves them clear.
Destroying the object removes the panes on the next commit; the blur region stays until the client unsets it.

entry.name: regular
entry.summary: menus, Control Center, the launcher, banners, sheets

entry.name: invalid_panes
entry.summary: the array is not whole panes, or a pane is malformed

request.name: set_panes
request.description:
Replace the surface's panes with `panes`: whole panes of seven 32-bit words each, in the host's byte order (as xdg_toplevel's states array), one after another:
x, y, width, height int: surface-local logical coordinates radius uint: corner radius in logical pixels, the same at all four corners; the compositor clamps it to half the shorter side material uint: a value of the material enum ink uint: the weakest words' colour on the pane, 0xAARRGGBB, for the contrast floor; 0 means the material's own ink
Panes are listed back to front: a later pane is drawn over an earlier one, and sees it frosted. An empty array is no panes.
Double-buffered: applied on the next wl_surface.commit, with the buffer and the blur region of that commit, so the glass always has the shape of the frame that shows. The panes stay until set again.
An array whose size is not a multiple of 28 bytes, a negative width or height, or a material outside the enum is an invalid_panes protocol error. A pane of zero width or height is ignored.

event.name: tone
event.description: The mean colour of what is behind the surface's panes, blurred and saturated as drawn, 0xFFRRGGBB, so the client can lean the colour of its words on glass toward it. Sent when it settles after a change, at most once every 120 ms; a compositor may never send it.
